'''How to Start Mining''' covers a commander's first ship-based mining run. [[Laser Mining|Laser mining]] is the most direct starting method because it uses the fewest specialist tools. Core, subsurface and surface-deposit mining require different hardpoints and are better approached after learning this basic collection loop.<ref>[https://www.elitedangerous.com/en-US/news/elite-dangerous-beyond-chapter-four-out-now Elite Dangerous: Beyond – Chapter Four – Out Now]. Frontier Developments. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

== Before departure ==

# Prepare the starter mining fit. At minimum, carry a [[Mining Laser]], [[Refinery]], [[Cargo Rack]], [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] and [[Collector Limpet Controller]]. Add a [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] when using mapped ring hotspots.
# Buy limpets from '''Advanced Maintenance → Restock''' before leaving the station. Limpets occupy cargo space as one-tonne units but are consumed during the trip, freeing that space for mined commodities.
# Choose a commodity and identify a suitable planetary ring. Check the receiving market before departure; prices and demand can change before the return trip.

A prospector identifies an asteroid's contents and increases the number of fragments released while the limpet remains attached, so it is part of the normal laser-mining loop rather than an optional scanner.<ref>[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Prospector_Limpet_Controller Prospector Limpet Controller]. ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

== Procedure ==

# Travel to the chosen ring. If targeting a hotspot, follow [[How to Scan Planetary Rings for Mining Hotspots]] and drop within the hotspot's highlighted area.
# Move clear of the arrival point and assess local contacts before deploying equipment. Resource Extraction Sites and ordinary hotspots are not the same thing; a hotspot does not require entering a RES.
# Deploy hardpoints and open the cargo scoop. Launch a prospector at an asteroid, target the attached limpet and inspect the listed commodities.
# If the asteroid contains the wanted resource, bring the mining lasers into range and fire until fragments are released.
# Launch collector limpets with no fragment targeted. An untargeted collector continues gathering nearby valid cargo, whereas a collector launched with a fragment targeted retrieves that item and then expires.<ref>[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Collector_Limpet_Controller Collector Limpet Controller]. ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
# Allow the collectors to deliver fragments through the cargo scoop. The refinery sorts the contents into bins and moves each completed tonne into the cargo hold automatically.<ref>[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Refinery Refinery]. ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
# Repeat the prospecting, extraction and collection cycle until the cargo hold is full, limpets run low or the planned session is complete.
# Return to a station with a commodities market and sell the refined cargo. Compare demand as well as the displayed unit price before committing a large load.

== During the run ==

* Ignore low-value resources through the Contacts panel by following [[How to Ignore Unwanted Mining Commodities]]. Filtering prevents collectors from repeatedly retrieving unwanted fragments.
* If every refinery bin is occupied or a completed tonne cannot enter the hold, follow [[How to Resolve a Full Refinery]].
* Raw engineering materials do not use refinery bins or cargo capacity; the material-storage notification is separate from refined commodity cargo.
* A hotspot increases the likelihood of its named commodity but does not guarantee that every asteroid will contain it.
* Stop before the final limpet is consumed if one is needed to retrieve the last fragments already in space.

== Choosing another mining method ==

Laser mining removes surface material directly with mining lasers. Other deposit types use the tools revealed by a prospector:<ref>[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Miner Miner]. ''Elite Dangerous Wiki''. Accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

* [[How to Mine Surface Deposits|Surface deposits]] require an [[Abrasion Blaster]].
* Subsurface deposits require a [[Sub-surface Displacement Missile]].
* Asteroid cores require a [[Seismic Charge Launcher]], followed by an abrasion blaster for the exposed deposits.

These methods can share the same refinery and collection support modules, but their search and extraction steps are distinct from the starter laser-mining procedure.
